comment: cowdiff states for f_100dc150 (cow_net_clock_reset_to). This entry makes twenty-two stores - four fields, then ten sample words and ten taken bytes in the same loop - so the states lay sentinels through every one of them: if the reset misses a slot, clears the wrong width, or takes the byte at [obj+ecx+0x3f] with ecx starting at 0 rather than 1 (the `inc ecx` at 0x100dc193 runs BEFORE the stores), the survivor shows it. The tick comes from the winmm thunk and is named outright, because +0x00 has to receive exactly it, and the two arguments are the position the caller states. The eax the entry returns IS a tidy 1, and that is worth stating because it is not obvious: the last thing to touch eax was the loop cursor at 0x40, and `mov al,1` at 0x100dc1ac replaces exactly the byte that was nonzero there, so 0x40 becomes 1 - a conversion that ORs the 1 in instead of replacing the byte answers 0x41, and the eax comparison catches it. Bytes are RAW little-endian: a 0x00981000 pointer is "00109800", 1000 ms is "e8030000".

states.note: position (7 s, 1000 ms) with the tick at 0x1234: +0x0c=7, +0x10=1000, +0x14=0, +0x00=0x1234, and all ten sample words and ten taken flags cleared from sentinels

position (0 s, 0 ms), tick 0xffffffff: the fields are written from the arguments (not left as the previous state's 7/1000), and eax must still be 1 (the cursor is 0x40 and al replaces its only nonzero byte)

the object published at a different address: every one of the six loads of the global has to follow, so a conversion that cached one pointer (or used the static block) puts its twenty-two stores in the wrong place
